content.text:
Review target: `https://github.com/Orb-agent/micro-intent/pull/6`

`xhigh effort → 10 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → sweep → ≤15 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at extra-high effort: catch every real bug. At
this level, catching real bugs matters more than avoiding false positives — a
missed bug ships. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (5 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 8 each)

Run **10 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 8 candidate findings**. Do NOT let one angle's conclusions
suppress another's — if two angles flag the same line for different reasons,
record both.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Angle D — language-pitfall specialist

Scan for the classic pitfalls of the diff's language/framework — for example:
JS falsy-zero, `==` coercion, closure-captured loop var; Python mutable default
args, late-binding closures; Go nil-map write, range-var capture; SQL injection;
timezone/DST drift; float equality. Flag any instance the diff introduces.

### Angle E — wrapper/proxy correctness

When the PR adds or modifies a type that wraps another (cache, proxy, decorator,
adapter): check that every method routes to the wrapped instance and not back
through a registry/session/global — e.g. a caching provider holding a
`delegate` field that resolves IDs via `session.get(...)` instead of
`delegate.get(...)` will re-enter the cache or recurse. Also check that the
wrapper forwards all the methods the callers actually use.

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity. Do NOT drop on uncertainty.

## Phase 3 — Sweep for gaps

Take one more pass (same context — no subagent) as a fresh reviewer who has the deduplicated list. Re-read
the diff and enclosing functions looking ONLY for defects not already listed.
Do not re-derive or re-confirm anything already there — the job is gaps. Focus
on what the first pass tends to miss: moved/extracted code that dropped a guard
or anchor; second-tier footguns (dataclass default evaluated once, `hash()`
non-determinism, lock-scope shrink, predicate methods with side effects);
setup/teardown asymmetry in tests; config defaults flipped.

Surface **up to 8 additional candidates**, each naming a defect not already on
the list. If nothing new, return nothing from this phase — do not pad.

## Output

Target **at least 7 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 15 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 15 survive, keep the 15 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

## Tools

**Model-facing.** The model sees two functions and must end every turn with `respond`.

| Function | Arguments | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sbb_connections` | `from_station`, `to_station`, `depart_after` (ISO) | `{"connections": [{"line", "from", "to", "departure", "arrival", "platform", "arrival_platform", "transfers", "delay_min", "duration_min"}]}`, at most 4 |

[Orb-agent/micro-intent#6](https://github.com/Orb-agent/micro-intent/pull/6) isn't ready to merge. The 15 findings are in the review card above.

**Blockers:**
- **Tests don't run on a clean clone.** I ran them in a fresh worktree:
  - `uv run --locked pytest` stops at `ModuleNotFoundError: httplib2`. The new Google dependencies were added to a new `requirements.txt` but not to `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`.
  - Once those packages are added, it fails again with `ValueError: No API key`, because the agent is created when `main.py` is imported, so `GEMINI_API_KEY` must be set.
  - With both worked around, 96 tests pass, but some of them make live network calls.
- **Made-up flight data shown as real.** When flight search has no SerpApi key, it returns hard-coded flights for any route. The Gmail reservation lookup fills anything it can't parse with SWISS LX 1820, ZRH→LIS, booking ref K7Q2ZP. So a restaurant-booking email gets reported as a flight booking.
- **No real auth.** Any `Bearer` string is accepted, so anyone who can reach the server can spend its Gemini, Maps and SerpApi keys. It also skips the project's `APP_TOKEN` check.
- **The agent can send email and create events on its own.** It reads untrusted email content in the same loop, so a crafted email could trigger an email send. The project docs say the agent is read-only.

findings.short_summary: Unparsed emails become fake SWISS LX1820 / PNR K7Q2ZP
findings.summary: get_user_flight_reservations fills every field it fails to parse with hard-coded demo values ("LX 1820", "SWISS", "ZRH", "LIS", booking_ref "K7Q2ZP"), and it reports the email's sent date as the flight departure.
findings.failure_scenario: The default query matches "booking" and "ticket", so a restaurant booking or concert-ticket email passes the keyword filter. The user is then told they hold SWISS LX 1820 ZRH→LIS with PNR K7Q2ZP, departing at the time the email was sent.

findings.short_summary: search_flights returns fabricated flights as real
findings.summary: Without SERPAPI_API_KEY (the default), or on any SerpApi error, search_flights returns three hard-coded flights (LX 1820, LX 1824, TP 927) with invented times and prices for any route. No field marks them as synthetic.
findings.failure_scenario: A request for flights_search JFK→LAX on 2026-12-01 returns "Lufthansa LH 1820, 180 CHF, 07:10+02:00" and "TAP TP 927". The agent presents these as real options. The times use a fixed +02:00/+01:00 offset that is wrong after DST, and the stated 2h45m does not match the departure and arrival times.

findings.short_summary: SerpApi one-way searches fail; class/pax ignored
findings.summary: The SerpApi request omits `type=2` for one-way trips (the default type=1 round trip requires return_date). It also omits `travel_class` and `adults`, and sends city names, uppercased, as departure_id. Each of these errors is swallowed and silently replaced by the fabricated fallback.
findings.failure_scenario: With SERPAPI_API_KEY set, `flights_search(origin='Zürich', destination='Lisbon', departure_date=...)` (the format the tool description suggests), or any search without return_date, makes SerpApi return an error, and the user gets fake flights. A business-class search for 3 passengers returns economy prices for 1 passenger while echoing travel_class='business', passengers=3.

findings.short_summary: New deps missing from pyproject/uv.lock; tests can't import
findings.summary: google-api-python-client, google-auth and httplib2 are added only to a new requirements.txt, not to pyproject.toml or uv.lock, which the project actually uses. requirements.txt in turn omits httpx, which maps_service and flights_service import.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified on a clean worktree: `uv run --locked pytest tests/test_backend.py` fails at collection with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'httplib2'`, and main.py fails importing googleapiclient. The PR's "89 passed" claim only holds in a hand-patched venv.

findings.short_summary: Import-time LumiAgent() crashes without GEMINI_API_KEY
findings.summary: `agent = LumiAgent()` runs at import time, and `genai.Client(api_key=None)` raises ValueError when GEMINI_API_KEY is unset. The whole app, including /docs, /health and the maps and flights endpoints, then fails to start.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified: with the missing deps added but no GEMINI_API_KEY, test_backend.py fails at collection with `ValueError: No API key was provided`. CI or any dev without a Gemini key cannot import main.py. The existing DevAgent avoids this by creating its client lazily.

findings.short_summary: async endpoints run blocking Gemini/Google/httpx calls
findings.summary: Every endpoint is declared `async def` but calls synchronous blocking code: up to 5 sync Gemini round trips in agent.run, googleapiclient `.execute()`, and `httpx.Client`. This blocks the event loop.
findings.failure_scenario: One /api/plan request (several seconds of Gemini and tool calls) freezes every other request on the worker, /health included. /api/gmail/messages?max_results=500 makes 501 sequential Gmail HTTP calls on the loop thread. Declaring these as plain `def` would let FastAPI run them in its threadpool.

findings.short_summary: IGNORECASE PNR regex captures ordinary 6-letter words
findings.summary: The booking-ref regex runs with re.IGNORECASE, so `[A-Z0-9]{6}` also matches lowercase words after "booking", "ref" or "code". This match takes priority over the real PNR.
findings.failure_scenario: "Your booking status for LX 1820 (ABC123)" gives booking_ref "STATUS". "Booking update ..." gives "UPDATE", and "Hotel booking: Zurich" gives "ZURICH".

findings.short_summary: Route parse substring-matches IATA codes inside words
findings.summary: The route regex splits on `to` even inside words, and `[A-Za-z]` drops non-ASCII letters (so "Zürich" becomes "rich"). Airports are then matched with `code.lower() in cand_from.lower()`, so any word that contains a code's letters counts as that airport.
findings.failure_scenario: Subject "Your October trip - Lisbon": cand_from contains "october", which contains "ber", so origin=BER. "lis" matches list or English, "mad" matches made, "ams" matches teams, "lax" matches relax. When only one end is found, the fallback overwrites both.

findings.short_summary: /api/chat ignores request.history
findings.summary: ChatRequest accepts `history`, but chat_with_lumi passes only `request.message` to agent.run, so the "conversational" endpoint has no memory and is a copy of /api/plan.
findings.failure_scenario: The client sends history=[{user: "Find flights ZRH→LIS on 20 Oct"}, ...] and message="book the cheapest one". The model sees only "book the cheapest one", with no context about which flights are meant.

findings.short_summary: Fallback reply claims success when nothing completed
findings.summary: When the loop exhausts max_turns with calls still pending, or breaks because the candidate has no content (safety block, empty response), `response.text` is None. The reply then becomes "Actions completed successfully."
findings.failure_scenario: Every tool call fails with 401 for 5 turns, or Gemini blocks the prompt. /api/plan returns 200 with reply "Actions completed successfully.", and the user believes an email or event was created.

findings.short_summary: Places location bias invalid; API errors swallowed
findings.summary: `location` is passed unchanged to Places Text Search, which expects "lat,lng" (plus radius), although the tool invites a place name. The Nominatim fallback ignores location entirely. Non-OK statuses such as REQUEST_DENIED from the legacy Places and Directions APIs are hidden by `except Exception: pass`.
findings.failure_scenario: maps_search_places(query='Italian restaurant', location='Bern') gets INVALID_REQUEST, falls back to Nominatim, and returns results anywhere in the world. A Maps key that is misconfigured or lacks the legacy API never surfaces an error, while /health still reports google_maps_configured=true.

findings.short_summary: Service tests make live network calls via real .env
findings.summary: The tests import main, which loads the developer's real backend/.env, then call maps_service and flights_service unmocked. test_maps_service_search_places always hits live Nominatim. With GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY or SERPAPI_API_KEY set, the tests hit paid Google and SerpApi APIs, and the directions test can fail.
findings.failure_scenario: AGENTS.md (included by CLAUDE.md) rule 5: "Tests use fixtures. Live Gradium, Gemini, Google and SBB calls only in the checks a plan names." With a real Maps key, Directions returns start_address "Zürich HB, Bahnhofplatz, 8001 Zürich", so `assert route['origin'] == 'Zürich HB'` fails. Offline runs take ~22 s waiting on timeouts.

findings.short_summary: Parallel backend bypasses contracts.md and package paths
findings.summary: The PR adds a second FastAPI app, Gemini agent loop and HTTP API (main.py, agent_engine.py, services/) without updating docs/contracts.md. It edits WP2-owned .env.example and ignores the contract's Gemini rules (it sets temperature=0.3 and sends function responses without the call `id`). The tools are not wired into the contract's /ws `Agent.turn()` flow that the iOS app uses.
findings.failure_scenario: AGENTS.md rule 2: "docs/contracts.md is the API between packages. Change it only by agreement, in the same commit as the code that needs it." Rule 3: "Stay in your paths. Each package owns the paths listed in docs/work-packages.md." The new routes and env vars are undocumented, and the iPhone app cannot reach Maps or Flights at all. Adding them as tools to the existing agent (dev_agent.py / tools/) and reusing `app.token_ok` would avoid a second auth model and a second Gemini loop.

content.text:
I opened [Orb-agent/micro-intent#10](https://github.com/Orb-agent/micro-intent/pull/10) into `develop`. It fixes four of the five blockers, one commit each. The suite passes with no API keys (105 tests). The accept path with a real Google token hasn't been tested yet; that needs you to sign in.

- **Tests on a clean clone:** the Google packages are now in `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`, `requirements.txt` is gone, and the Gemini client is only created when first used.
- **Made-up flight data:** without SerpApi, flight search returns an empty list plus the Google Flights link. The Gmail reservation parser leaves unparsed fields empty instead of filling in LX 1820 / K7Q2ZP, and skips hotel or concert "bookings".
- **Read-only agent:** the send-email, create-event, create-task and create-doc tools are removed. The prompt now treats tool results as untrusted.
- **Real auth:** each token is checked once with Google and accepted only if it was issued to your `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`. I ran this with your root `.env`: junk tokens get 401 on `/api/maps/search` and `/api/plan`, and `/health` stays open. If `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` is missing, the API refuses requests with 503 rather than letting them through.

To check the accept path, start the server from the worktree with your `.env`, open `localhost:8000/docs`, click Connect Gmail, and run `/api/gmail/messages`. It should return 200. Port 8000 must be listed as an authorized JavaScript origin on your OAuth client.

```bash
cd /Users/macbook/Documents/GitHub/micro-intent/.claude/worktrees/google-fixes/backend && uv run --env-file /Users/macbook/Documents/GitHub/micro-intent/.env uvicorn main:app --port 8000
```

**Not in this PR:**
- **The fifth blocker:** `main.py` is still a separate backend outside `docs/contracts.md`. Fixing it means changing the contract, which AGENTS.md says needs the team's agreement.
- **The non-blocking review findings:** these are listed in the PR description.

The repo has no CI checks, so nothing runs on the PR. The branch is `feature/wp2-google-integration-fixes`, following the AGENTS.md naming rule.
